HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #13
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: HISTORY AND CITIZENSHIP MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which statement about Colonialism in Contemporary Society is most accurate for CBC learning? (1 mark)
   A. Treat Colonialism in Contemporary Society as rumours only.
   B. Skip evidence when discussing Colonialism in Contemporary Society.
   C. Say Colonialism in Contemporary Society never happens in Kenya.
   D. Explain Colonialism in Contemporary Society with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

   D. Skip evidence when discussing Critical Issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship.

   D. Explain Implementation of the Constitution of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

7. Citizenship responsibility includes: (1 mark)
   A. Littering in markets
   B. Destroying road signs
   C. Avoiding all community work
   D. Obeying laws and caring for public property

12. Kenya’s capital city is: (1 mark)
   A. Nakuru
   B. Mombasa
   C. Kisumu
   D. Nairobi

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Conflict Resolutions in Independent Africa and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain The Russian Revolution and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain International Organisations and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

====

1. D — Explain Colonialism in Contemporary Society with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

2. B — Explain Critical Issues in Kenyan History and Citizenship with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

3. C — Explain Themes in African History and Citizenship 2.3 Social, Economic and Political cha with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

4. D — Explain External Security with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

5. D — Explain Contemporary migrations, settlements and expansion in Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

6. D — Explain Implementation of the Constitution of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

7. D — Obeying laws and caring for public property

8. D — Explain Major Economic developments and challenges in Kenya since independence with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

9. B — Explain symbols used on a map

10. A — Explain Structure and functions of the National Government of Kenya with correct facts and a clear Kenyan example.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Conflict Resolutions in Independent Africa; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of International Organisations; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
